div.head: Abt 26[a]
div.ab: Gif læt ofslæhð, þone selestan LXXX scll' forgelde;
Gif læt ofslæhð, þone selastan LXXX scƚƚ forgelde.
If [a person] kills a freedman of the first rank, let him pay [with] 80 shillings
If he slays a læt of the best class, he shall pay 80 shillings;
If [anyone] kills a læt, he is to pay for one of the highest class 80 shillings; if he kills one of the second class, he is to pay 60 shillings; if one of the third class, he is to pay 40 shillings.
Wenn [jemand] einen Halbfreien erschlägt, entgelte er den [an Range] vorzüglichsten mit 80 Schll.;
If [someone] slays a half-free man, let him pay for the most excellent [in rank] with 80 shillings;
div.note: Only in Kent is there reference to this class, lower than the ceorl, but above the slave. Liebermann translates “half-free”. A læt may be a manumitted slave, or perhaps a member of a subject (pre- English) population.
Whitelock translates Abt 26 as one clause, which the sheet divides into rows 26[a], 26[b], 26[c]; her translation of the whole is given here, in the first row.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Læt 3; nichts damit hat lathe (s. d. Gl) zu tun noch litorum ‘Küstengestade’ in Urk. Bi 880. D. v. Kralik deutet das Wort: ‘[im Besitz der Ländereien] Gelassener’; Neues Archiv ält. Dt. Geschi. 38 (1913), 436

Cf. Gl Læt 3; lathe (see that word in Gl) has nothing to do with it, nor has litorum ‘coastal shores’ in charter Bi 880. D. v. Kralik interprets the word: ‘one left [in possession of the lands]’; Neues Archiv ält. Dt. Geschi. 38 (1913), 436

Nicht bloss das für ‘Schutz’ an den Herrn, sondern alles für den Erschlagenen zu Zahlende ist laut der hohen Summe gemeint. Da aber forgieldan sowohl Sachen und Unfreie (Abt 12. 4) wie Wergeld Freier (Abt 7. 22f.) zum Objekt haben kann, erhellt nicht, wer das Geld empfing und ob es Wergeld (s. d. Gl 1) darstellt

Not merely what is to be paid for ‘protection’ to the lord, but everything to be paid for the slain man is meant, to judge from the high sum. But since forgieldan can have as its object both things and unfree persons (Abt 12. 4) and the wergild of free men (Abt 7. 22f.), it is not clear who received the money and whether it represents wergild (see that word in Gl 1)

Die drei Klassen und ihren Entgelt findet Seebohm (Tribal custom in AgSax. law 484) genau wieder in denen der Nordischen Freigelassenen; je nach dem Grade, in welchem sie der Vollfreiheit näher standen, meint er also, unterschieden sich auch die Agsächs. Læten. Doch kann (und die Analogie mit dem Walliser in Wessex führt darauf) auch die wirtschaftliche Verschiedenheit, der Grundbesitz, die Klassifizierung begründen

The three classes and their price Seebohm (Tribal custom in AgSax. law 484) finds exactly again in those of the Nordic freedmen; according to the degree in which they stood nearer to full freedom, so he thinks, the A.-S. læts also differed among themselves. But (and the analogy with the Welshman in Wessex points to this) the economic difference, landed property, may also be the ground of the classification
